pack.topic: Plinth Beam vs Lintel Beam Structural Coordination
pack.source_script_insight: The source video explains the mechanical coordination between a lower component (crankshaft for base power) and an upper component (camshaft for opening/closing control), linked together to ensure structural/operational harmony.
pack.coimbatore_angle: Coimbatore's varied soil profiles (from red soil in Saravanampatti to clayey tracts in Singanallur) demand strict coordination between the bottom plinth beam and top lintel beam to prevent structural settlement cracks above door frames.
pack.core_takeaway: A home needs both a bottom plinth beam to distribute foundation load and a top lintel beam to support masonry over openings, structurally tied by columns to prevent wall cracks.
pack.voiceover_tamil: கதவு மேல் விரிசல் வரக்கூடாதா? கீழே பிளின்த், மேலே லிண்டல்! இரண்டும் இணைந்தால் தான் பலம்! ஆலிவ்ட்ரீ பில்டர்ஸ்!

scenes.purpose: Establish the problem (visual hook of structural failure)
scenes.visual: Close-up of a diagonal crack in interior plaster running from the top corner of a wooden door frame upward through red brick masonry.
scenes.camera: Static close-up, eye-level, sharp focus on the plaster crack texture.

scenes.purpose: Introduce the lower structural component (Plinth Beam)
scenes.visual: Low-angle shot of a freshly cast concrete plinth beam at ground level, showing the rough wooden shuttering boards and damp earth.
scenes.camera: Slow tilt-down to ground level, showcasing the horizontal concrete beam.

scenes.purpose: Introduce the upper structural component (Lintel Beam)
scenes.visual: Eye-level shot tilting up to a solid concrete lintel beam cast directly over a door opening, with red clay bricks stacked above it.
scenes.camera: Smooth tilt-up from door height to the lintel beam level.

scenes.purpose: Show the physical connection (Columns acting like the timing linkage)
scenes.visual: A Coimbatore construction worker tying steel stirrups on a vertical column rebar cage that connects the lower plinth level to the upper lintel level.
scenes.camera: Medium shot, tracking the worker's hands using binding wire.

scenes.purpose: Explain the lower component's function (Preventing settlement)
scenes.visual: Close-up of the cured concrete surface of the plinth beam, showing strong aggregate distribution resisting soil movement.
scenes.camera: Slow pan across the horizontal concrete texture.

scenes.purpose: Explain the upper component's function (Supporting load over openings)
scenes.visual: Close-up of the lintel beam cleanly transferring the weight of the heavy red brick wall above it away from the door frame below.
scenes.camera: Static medium close-up, highlighting the interface between concrete and brick.

scenes.visual: A clean, structurally complete residential frame under bright Coimbatore sunlight, with coconut palms visible in the background.
scenes.camera: Slight gimbal push-forward, wide shot of the secure structure.

pack.gemini_video_prompt:
Create a highly realistic, production-grade 10-second video for OliveTree Builders, focused strictly on Coimbatore residential construction. The video must consist of exactly 7 scenes, formatted in a native 9:16 portrait ratio. The entire video must look like photorealistic live-action smartphone or gimbal footage captured on active construction sites in Tamil Nadu. No 3D animations, cartoon explainers, or flat vector graphics are allowed. Motion graphics are strictly limited to simple, clean text overlays. 

Scene 1 (0.0-1.4s): Close-up of a diagonal structural crack in interior wall plaster spreading from the top corner of a wooden door frame. Natural morning light casting soft shadows. Text overlay: 'CRACKS ABOVE DOORS?'. VO: 'கதவு மேல் விரிசல் வரக்கூடாதா?'
Scene 2 (1.4-2.8s): Low-angle shot of a freshly cast concrete plinth beam at ground level. Wet concrete texture, wooden shuttering boards, and local red soil visible. Text overlay: 'PLINTH AT BOTTOM'. VO: 'கீழே பிளின்த்,'
Scene 3 (2.8-4.2s): Eye-level shot tilting up to a solid concrete lintel beam cast directly over a door frame opening with red clay bricks above it. Text overlay: 'LINTEL AT TOP'. VO: 'மேலே லிண்டல்!'
Scene 4 (4.2-5.6s): Medium shot of a construction worker in Coimbatore tying steel stirrups on a vertical column rebar cage that connects the lower plinth level to the upper lintel level. Text overlay: 'TIED BY COLUMNS'. VO: 'இரண்டும் இணைந்தால் தான் பலம்!'
Scene 5 (5.6-7.0s): Close-up of the cured concrete surface of the plinth beam, showing strong aggregate distribution resisting soil movement. Text overlay: 'STOPS SETTLEMENT'. VO: 'அடித்தளம் இறங்குவதை'
Scene 6 (7.0-8.5s): Close-up of the lintel beam cleanly transferring the weight of the heavy red brick wall above it away from the door frame below. Text overlay: 'HOLDS WALL LOAD'. VO: 'தடுத்து, சுவரை தாங்கும்!'
Scene 7 (8.5-10.0s): Wide shot of a structurally sound, newly framed house under bright Coimbatore sunlight, with coconut palms in the background. Text overlay: 'BUILD WITH OLIVETREE'. VO: 'ஆலிவ்ட்ரீ பில்டர்ஸ்!'

Ensure visual continuity across all scenes with consistent daylight, realistic local Coimbatore red clay bricks, and standard Indian site conditions. 

NEGATIVE PROMPT: Do not include any 3D CAD models, cartoon animations, flat vector graphics, white background infographics, glossy corporate motion graphics, game-like 3D renders, plastic CGI, floating documents, or impossible camera movements. No generic stock footage from outside India. No text outside the specified overlays.
pack.title_english: Why You Need Both Plinth & Lintel Beams
pack.caption_english: Ever noticed cracks appearing right above your doors or windows? This happens when the structural load isn't distributed correctly. Just like an engine needs both a crankshaft at the bottom and a camshaft at the top to run smoothly, your home needs a Plinth Beam at the foundation level and a Lintel Beam above openings. Tied together by vertical columns, they prevent soil settlement and protect your walls from cracking. In Coimbatore's diverse soil conditions, skipping either is a major risk. Build your home with structural integrity. Contact OliveTree Builders today to plan your strong, crack-free home!
